title: [Activity] Bleeding Edge Alert! Mise en Scene Recommendations

cues.en: Time for our first bleeding edge alert.
cues.zh: 第一次前沿研究提醒登場。

cues.en: This is where we highlight some new research that looks interesting or promising, but hasn't really made it into the mainstream yet with recommender systems.
cues.zh: 這個環節會介紹一些有趣或有潛力、但還沒在推薦系統領域成為主流的新研究。

cues.en: We want you to have all the latest and greatest information in this course.
cues.zh: 我們希望這門課能帶給你最新、最好的資訊。

cues.en: If you're not familiar with the term, we often refer to the current state of the art as leading edge, but technology that's still so new that it's unproven in the real world can be risky
cues.zh: 如果不熟悉這個用語，我們常把目前最先進的技術稱為 leading edge；但有些技術太新，還沒在真實世界驗證，使用時可能有風險，

cues.en: to work with and so we call that bleeding edge.
cues.zh: 所以稱為 bleeding edge，也就是尚待驗證的前沿技術。

cues.en: Some recent research and content based filtering has surrounded the use of mise en scene data.
cues.zh: 最近一些內容式過濾研究，探討了場面調度，也就是 mise en scène 資料的運用。

cues.en: Technically, mise en scene refers to the placement of objects in a scene, but the researchers are using this term a bit more loosely to refer to the properties of the scenes in a movie or movie trailer.
cues.zh: 嚴格來說，場面調度指場景中物體的安排，但研究者用得比較寬鬆，泛指電影或預告片中場景的特性。

cues.en: The idea is to extract properties from the film itself that can be quantified and analyzed and see if we can come up with better movie recommendations by examining the content of the movie itself scene by scene.
cues.zh: 概念是，從影片本身擷取可量化、可分析的特性，逐一檢視場景內容，看看能否產生更好的電影推薦。

cues.en: What sort of attributes are we talking about?
cues.zh: 談的是哪些屬性？

cues.en: Here's the list of attributes that the research team extracted for a movie trailers associated with the movie lens data set.
cues.zh: 這是研究團隊從與 MovieLens 資料集對應的電影預告片中，擷取的屬性清單。

cues.en: It includes things like average shot length, color variance, how much motion is in each scene, how scenes are lit, and things like that.
cues.zh: 包括平均鏡頭長度、色彩變異、每個場景有多少動作、場景如何打光等等。

cues.en: So in principle, this should give us a feel as to the pacing and mood of the film just based on the film itself.
cues.zh: 因此，原則上應該能只根據電影本身，了解它的節奏與氛圍。

cues.en: The question is whether this data is more or less useful than the human generated genre classifications we've already been using for each film.
cues.zh: 問題是，這些資料比我們一直使用、由人類產生的電影類型分類，更有用還是更沒用？

cues.en: Well, let's find out.
cues.zh: 來找答案。

cues.en: Let's take another look at content KNN algorithm dot PY and have a look at the compute mise en scene similarity function.
cues.zh: 再看看 ContentKNNAlgorithm.py 裡的 computeMiseEnSceneSimilarity 函數。

cues.en: Just like we can compute similarity scores based on genres and release years, we can also compute similarity scores based on this mise on scene data.
cues.zh: 就像可以根據類型與上映年份計算相似度，也能根據場面調度資料計算相似度。

cues.en: How we chose to do that is a bit arbitrary.
cues.zh: 選擇的計算方法，有一點主觀。

cues.en: We're just taking the absolute difference between these properties between each pair of movies and multiplying them together.
cues.zh: 我們只計算每對電影之間各屬性差異的絕對值，再把它們相乘。

cues.en: There are probably better ways of doing it, but before we spend of bunch of time fine-tuning it, let's just try this out and see if using this data at all does more good than harm.
cues.zh: 可能有更好的方法，但在花很多時間微調之前，先試試看使用這份資料，究竟利大於弊還是弊大於利。

cues.en: The code that actually codes and parses the mise en scene data we have is in the movie lens dot PY module.
cues.zh: 實際載入並解析場面調度資料的程式碼，在 MovieLens.py 模組中。

cues.en: It's not terribly important how that works, but you can go look at it if you're curious.
cues.zh: 它如何運作不是非常重要，但有興趣可以看看。

cues.en: Now remember our RMSE score from using genres and years was point nine three seven five and our sample top end recommendations were kind of uninspiring.
cues.zh: 記得，使用類型與年份時，RMSE 是 0.9375，抽看的 Top-N 推薦也不太令人振奮。

cues.en: Let's put mise en scene data into the mix and see what happens.
cues.zh: 加入場面調度資料，看看結果。

cues.en: To do that, just uncomment line 45
cues.zh: 只要取消第 45 行的註解，

cues.en: to commute that mise en scene similarity score and multitply it in on line 46 like so.
cues.zh: 計算場面調度相似度，再像這樣於第 46 行乘進去。

cues.en: Let's run it and see what happens.
cues.zh: 執行看看會發生什麼事。

cues.en: Save it, select content rex dot PY and run it.
cues.zh: 儲存，選取 ContentRecs.py，再執行。

cues.en: Again, if you're playing along, hit pause and resume when it's done in a few minutes.
cues.zh: 同樣地，如果跟著操作，先暫停，等幾分鐘完成後再繼續。

cues.en: Okay, so that's interesting, our RMSE actually got a lot worse, rising to over one point zero.
cues.zh: 好，有意思，RMSE 反而差了很多，升到 1.0 以上。

cues.en: Now, this could again just be an artifact of how we chose to compute mise en scene similarity scores.
cues.zh: 同樣地，這可能只是我們選擇的場面調度相似度計算方式造成的。

cues.en: Accuracy isn't really what we're concerned with, but do the top end recommendations look any better from a qualitative standpoint?
cues.zh: 準確程度不是真正在意的，但從品質角度來看，Top-N 推薦有比較好嗎？

cues.en: I don't know, it seems like it's recommending even more obscure stuff, although that new recommendation for a "Mission to Mars" seems interesting given this user's interest in a Star Trek movie.
cues.zh: 我也不確定，看起來推薦了更多冷門東西。不過，考量到這位使用者喜歡《星際爭霸戰》電影，新增的《火星任務》推薦似乎有意思。

cues.en: Again, sometimes developing recommendation systems is more an art than a science.
cues.zh: 再次強調，有時開發推薦系統，藝術成分多於科學。

cues.en: You can't really predict how real people will react to new recommendations they haven't seen before.
cues.zh: 你無法真正預測，真實使用者對以前沒看過的新推薦，會有什麼反應。

cues.en: Personally, I'd be tempted to test this in an AB test to see how it performs.
cues.zh: 我自己會想用 A/B 測試，看看它表現如何。

cues.en: If you look at the research literature associated with mise en scene recommendations however, they note that it doesn't do any favors to accuracy, but it does increase diversity.
cues.zh: 不過，場面調度推薦的研究文獻指出，它沒有改善準確程度，但確實提高多樣性。

cues.en: But again, increased diversity isn't always a good thing when it comes to recommendations.
cues.zh: 但再次強調，推薦的多樣性增加，不一定是好事。

cues.en: It may just mean that you're recommending random stuff that has no correlation to the user's actual interests.
cues.zh: 也可能只是推薦隨機項目，與使用者真正的興趣毫無關聯。

cues.en: Still it was interesting to experiment with it and it would be even more interesting to experiment with it using real people.
cues.zh: 不過，實驗它仍然很有趣，拿真實使用者測試，會更有趣。

cues.en: To give the required credit for the mise en scene data we're using and to give a pointer for learning more, here's a reference to the original research paper surrounding it and a link to where you
cues.zh: 為了註明場面調度資料的來源，也提供深入學習的方向，這裡列出原始研究論文的參考資訊，以及可以

cues.en: can explore the data set in more depth.
cues.zh: 進一步探索資料集的連結。

cues.en: You can see this is fairly recent research.
cues.zh: 可以看到，這是相當近期的研究。

cues.en: It's sort of bleeding edge stuff right now, but I want you to know about the most interesting latest developments in recommender systems as part of this course.
cues.zh: 目前還屬於前沿技術，不過我希望透過這門課，讓你知道推薦系統中最有趣的新發展。

cues.en: This won't be the last one we explore.
cues.zh: 這不會是我們探索的最後一項。
